station_overview.name: International Space Station
station_overview.tagline: A permanently inhabited laboratory in low Earth orbit.
station_overview.what_is_it: The ISS is a modular space station used for long-duration human habitation, research, technology demonstration, and international cooperation.
purpose: Preparation for future Moon and Mars missions

partners.role: Overall program leadership, U.S. Orbital Segment, operations, research, logistics
Russian Orbital Segment, propulsion, docking, attitude support, crew transport heritage
Columbus laboratory and European contributions through member states
Kibo laboratory and Japanese research systems

systems.title: Power System
systems.what_it_does: Generates, stores, and distributes electricity across the station.
systems.why_it_matters: Without power, life support, computing, science, lighting, communications, and thermal control are affected.

systems.title: Life Support
systems.what_it_does: Maintains breathable air, water recovery, pressure control, and habitability.
systems.why_it_matters: This system makes long-duration human life possible.

systems.title: Thermal Control
systems.what_it_does: Removes excess heat and keeps equipment and crew areas within safe temperature limits.
systems.why_it_matters: Spacecraft systems can overheat or freeze without thermal regulation.

systems.title: Robotics
systems.what_it_does: Supports assembly, capture, maintenance, and external operations.
systems.why_it_matters: Robotics reduce astronaut risk and extend what can be done outside the station.

timeline.title: Assembly begins
timeline.detail: The first ISS elements launched and on-orbit assembly started.

timeline.title: Continuous human occupation begins
timeline.detail: Crews began living aboard the station continuously.

timeline.title: Major U.S. laboratory capability expands
timeline.detail: Research and habitation capability grew as major modules were added.

timeline.title: Columbus and Kibo era
timeline.detail: European and Japanese laboratory capabilities expanded the station’s science role.
